title: Define nested toggle-group focus and validation protocols for inline forms
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Problem: Nested toggle groups (examples: payment frequency inside billing options, per-field feature flags, and grouped accessibility toggles) currently have inconsistent keyboard focus order, unclear validation anchoring, and unpredictable error messaging when a child toggle changes parent validation state. This leads to a11y gaps (screen reader confusion), keyboard-only users losing context, and flaky visual focus outlines in compact/inline forms.

Goal: Produce a single interaction protocol and set of implementation guidance for nested toggle groups used inside inline, multi-row forms. Deliverables: a design spec and annotated components that cover focus order, keyboard interactions, screen reader announcements (aria-live or aria-describedby), validation anchoring and error summarization behavior, visual focus and hover tokens, and RTL adaptations. The spec should be implementable by frontend and product teams and include examples for canary rollout in Console routes and Compact density forms.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard navigation: Tab/Shift+Tab moves between logical form controls; arrow keys move within a toggle group without escaping to parent controls unless at group boundary
Validation messages anchor to the nearest meaningful control and optionally to group label when group-level validation is present

Screen reader output: activating or toggling a child option that introduces a validation error triggers a concise announcement with context (control label + short error) without repeating form fields excessively
RTL behavior: visual focus ring and caret order mirror LTR expectations and arrow key mappings remain intuitive
Design tokens: focus/hover/active spacing and color tokens defined; compact vs regular density variants documented

Edge-case flow: when toggling a child clears or creates an async validation error (server-side), the UI shows a transient state, an inline spinner, and an unobtrusive toast only for global errors; the inline validation should be primary
notes: 2026-03-10 Sofia: Kicked off exploratory audit across Console routes that use nested toggles (billing, feature flags, dataset privacy). Noted 7 instances with inconsistent behavior across components library versions.

2026-03-11 Ethan: Built interactive prototype in Storybook that demonstrates three variants: flat toggles, grouped toggles with legend, and nested toggles with embedded fields. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web-ui/pull/1456

2026-03-11 UX research: Quick hallway tests with 5 participants (keyboard and screen-reader users). Observations: arrow-key expectations differ when group role is ambiguous; need clear group labeling and aria-roledescription; users expect Tab to move to next logical field, arrows to navigate within group only.

2026-03-12 Design decision: Use rolegroup + aria-labelledby for group semantics; implement arrow-key navigation within a roving tabindex pattern; use aria-live="polite" region for succinct validation updates and aria-describedby on controls for persistent helper/error text.

Trade-offs discussed: 1) Use of aria-live improves screen reader immediacy but may double-announce if form-level summary also exists; mitigation: only announce child-level errors inline and suppress duplicate summary announcement for the same error. 2) Roving tabindex adds JS complexity—will provide a small, well-documented utility in the component library to reduce duplication.

Implementation notes: Provide CSS-only focus outline for simple toggles but fall back to JS-managed focus for nested groups that require roving tabindex. Define an accessibility utility hook (useRovingTabindex) in the component library; engineering to own the hook and tests.
Follow-ups: Add unit tests to ensure arrow-key nav does not break with virtualization (large option lists). Add integration test coverage for async validation flows (mock server).
